note: Do the two kept optimizations compose? They target different stages -- the decoded-frame cache is in the renderer, the focal-search change is in the tracker -- so they ought to, but ought-to is not a measurement. All arms ran on one image containing both changes, selected by environment variable, so no bind-mounting is involved. IMPORTANT: RENDER_FRAME_CACHE is a frame COUNT, not a boolean; two earlier attempts at this test were void, the first because the image predated both changes and the second because the cache was set to 1, a size that misses on every frame. This is the third attempt.

baseline.note: The baseline from the SAME run as the treated arms, which is the correct paired reference. An earlier version of this section used j2off2 (395.52) from the previous run because j3base had not finished; the two differ by 0.61 % and the figures here were restated when it landed. j3base also ran LAST, so drift works against the treated arms rather than for them.

independentCacheMeasurement.note: measured separately, different image, bind-mounted file

independentFocalSaving.note: the CONFIRMED variant that actually ships, measured on this same image against its own baseline (j2on vs j2off2). The -9.61% published elsewhere is the unconfirmed variant on a patched image; both are real, and this is the one that composes here.

stagesNote: All three stage columns come from the same three arms as the wall-clock table, so nothing is borrowed from another experiment's baseline. paste_back_video is carried as a control: neither change touches it and it moves 0.1 s across all three arms.

outputSanity.note: check_video.py on all three arms: no near-black or flat frames, no frozen output, mouth motion present.

outputVsBaseline.note: At the build's own reproducibility floor -- two identical seeded runs share no bit-identical frames either -- so an end-to-end diff carries no information about either change. Both are output-neutral at the point of change instead, proven by unit test.
